key_insight: TACO achieves near-zero optimizer-state memory for LLM fine-tuning by using a column-wise one-sparse steepest-descent update under a dimension-normalized 1→1 operator norm.
engineering_relevance: It makes full-parameter fine-tuning of much larger models feasible on a single GPU by sharply reducing memory without sacrificing accuracy or runtime.
method: Selects the sign of the largest-magnitude entry in each column of 2D weight matrices.
Retains first-order gradients while storing only a small set of low-precision gradient components per column.
Follows Muon’s operator-norm steepest-descent view but further compresses the update geometry.
evidence_signal: On OPT-13B, TACO reduced persistent optimizer state from 27.7 GB to 0.16 GB and peak training memory from 80.6 GB to 27.5 GB, with comparable accuracy and runtime, and enabled fine-tuning of 30–32B models on a single 80 GB H100.
watch_item: The method is geometry-specific and relies on column-wise matrix structure, so implementation details and performance may vary for layers or training setups that do not fit this assumption.
paper_title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
